arms.predicted: v10 (unified sweep + early termination + fast I/O + random restart) will achieve a marginally higher mean score than v7 across 3 seeds (+1-3 points average). The improvement comes from unified allocation letting the primary sweep explore more widths, early termination making each pack() call ~10-20% faster, and random restart using idle time for ordering diversity.
arms.observed: v10 scores: 82.71, 82.81, 82.60 (mean 82.71, std 0.11). v7 scores: 81.14, 79.91, 85.07 (mean 82.04, std 2.70). Paired differences (v10-v7): +1.57, +2.91, -2.47 (mean +0.67, std 2.80). Paired t-test: t=0.415, p=0.719. Direction: v10 > v7 in 2/3 seeds. The mean improvement (+0.67 pts) is in the predicted direction but below the predicted range (+1-3 pts) and not statistically significant (p=0.719). However, v10 shows dramatically reduced variance: range 0.21 pts (82.60-82.81) vs v7's range 5.16 pts (79.91-85.07). This variance reduction is the dominant observable effect of v10's optimizations.
arms.diagnostic_note: The predicted mean improvement (+1-3 pts) was not achieved at statistical significance (observed +0.67, p=0.72). However, the direction is correct in 2/3 seeds and the variance reduction effect is striking: v10's unified time allocation and early termination make the score almost deterministic across runs (std=0.11 vs 2.70 for v7). This suggests the mechanism IS engaging — v10 explores widths more efficiently and consistently — but the mean benefit is smaller than predicted, likely because v7's Phase 2 (alt orderings at bestWidth ±3) provides genuine value for cases where the primary-ordering width-sweep misses the optimum. The random restart in v10 partially compensates but cannot fully replace the structured Phase 2 approach. The v10 variance reduction is important for deployment: a system that reliably scores 82.7 is more useful than one that swings between 80 and 85.

arms.predicted: v7 will score in the range 79-86 (mean ~83), consistent with iter-2 and iter-3 measurements.
arms.observed: v7 scores: 81.14, 79.91, 85.07 (mean 82.04, std 2.70). Range 79.91-85.07 is within the predicted 79-86 range. Mean (82.04) is close to the predicted ~83. Consistent with iter-2 (82.86 mean) and iter-3 (82.87 mean). The high variance (std 2.70, range 5.16) confirms RP-3: system-load-induced score variance ~6 points for the v7 time-managed width sweep.

discrepancy_analysis: The h-main prediction of +1-3 mean improvement was directionally correct but the magnitude was overstated. The observed +0.67 mean improvement is not statistically significant (p=0.72) with 3 seeds, given the high paired-difference variance (std=2.80) driven by v7's load sensitivity. The most notable finding is the dramatic VARIANCE REDUCTION in v10: std=0.11 vs std=2.70 for v7. This was not explicitly predicted but is a direct consequence of the hypothesized mechanism (faster pack calls → more widths explored → less sensitivity to exactly which widths fit in the time budget). The unified allocation eliminates the 60/40 time split's interaction with system load. The v7 baseline performed as expected (CONFIRMED), validating the experimental setup.
